title: How we treat plants and animals
intro: Allah made the plant and animal world serve us – and we must treat it with care and mercy.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html:
He is the One who created for you everything on the earth, then turned to the sky and made it seven heavens – and He knows everything. (Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:29, meaning)
He is the One who made the earth easy for you, so walk through its regions and eat from what He provides – and to Him you will be raised. (Qur’an, Al-Mulk 67:15, meaning)

One of the most important features of Islam is that it gives equal attention to the dunya – this world – and the akhirah – the world to come. Islam calls Muslims to work for a kind and caring society, and at the same time to try to enter Jannah by Allah’s mercy.
On that path we must always treat the plant and animal world, which Allah made to serve us, carefully and responsibly.

items: Plants are our greatest helper against harmful gases.
Green areas help to balance the winds and reduce noise.
Economic progress and development are closely tied to nature, where everything works in harmony and every result has its cause.

learn.html: Before we go out into nature we should learn the basic rules of behaving there. People often carry bad habits from home to picnic spots, parks, forests and mountains. Far from home there is often nowhere to put rubbish, and bins near towns are often full. Muslims should be an example of the right way to treat nature in every situation – for example, by taking their rubbish home with them.
Six surahs of the Qur’an are named after animals, and animals are mentioned in the Qur’an and hadiths in many places:
There is great wisdom in this. Many rules of the Shari‘ah are connected to animals – from eating their meat, to using them for hunting, to owning them.

learn.title: No pain without need
learn.html: We are forbidden to cause pain to other living beings, except in real necessity. By the rules of our religion we may kill pests that cause harm, but we may not torture any animal, and we may not burn them with fire, because that is a great sin.

learn.title: 📜 Hadith
learn.html: It is reported that one of the Companions said: “I went with my grandfather Anas ibn Malik (RA) to the house of Al-Hakam ibn Ayyub. There we saw some people using a hen as a target. Anas said to them: ‘The Messenger of Allah (SAW) forbade that any animal be tied up and used as a target.’” (Muslim)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Whoever shows mercy to a living being, the Creator will show mercy to him.

practice.title: Kind to every creature
practice.prompt: Tap everything a Muslim does, then tap Check.

options.text: Puts out food for birds in winter
Takes rubbish home after a picnic
Looks after trees and green areas
Removes pests that cause harm, without torturing them
Uses a hen or a cat as a target for fun
options.why: The Prophet (SAW) forbade tying up an animal and using it as a target.
Burning living beings with fire is a great sin.

options.text: Leaves rubbish in the forest because the bins are full
options.why: Muslims should be an example in nature – we take our rubbish with us.

questions.q: How many surahs are named after animals?
Which surah is named after the ant?

options: this world (dunya) and the next world (akhirah)

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) forbid, according to Anas ibn Malik (RA)?
options: Tying up an animal and using it as a target

questions.q: Who will the Creator show mercy to?
options: Whoever shows mercy to living beings
